premise: Clouds gather and everyone hurries home — Beaver to his lodge, Badger to his burrow, Bird to his nest — each worrying about Snail, who isn't hurrying at all, because his house is on his back.
inspiration: Zeus and the Tortoise (Aesop), where carrying your house is a punishment; turned: it's a gift, and Snail is the one who stays dry.
lesson: What makes you different can be exactly what you need.
learning: A snail carries its shell, its house, wherever it goes.

en-US.title: Snail Brought His House
en-US.text: {canvas:clouds 0.7} [rushed] Grey clouds rolled in. Rain was coming! Everyone hurried home. {beaver:enter} Beaver stopped by {snail:enter} Snail. {beaver:go to snail} {beaver:face surprised} "Snail! Where's your house?" {snail:face happy} {snail:live talk} "Right here," said Snail. But Beaver {beaver:live gnaw} gnawed him a stick for a roof. "Just in case," he said, and {beaver:go away} off he hurried to his lodge. {badger:enter} {badger:go to snail} Badger stopped by. {badger:face surprised} "Snail! Where's your house?" "Right here." But Badger {badger:live dig} dug him a little hole. "Just in case," he said, and {badger:go away} off he hurried to his burrow. {bird:enter} {bird:go to snail} Bird swooped down. {bird:face surprised} "Snail! Where's your house?" [giggles] {snail:live laugh} "Right HERE!" said Snail. {bird:go away} Off flew Bird to his nest. {canvas:rain 0.8} {sfx:rain} Pitter-patter, down came the rain. {snail:live hide hold} Snail tucked himself into his shell. {sfx:taps} Tap, tap, went the rain on his roof. {canvas:rain stop} {canvas:clouds stop} {canvas:sunshine} When the rain stopped and the sun came out, {beaver:go back} {badger:go back} {bird:go back} back came his friends. {badger:face sad} [gently] "Snail? Are you wet?" {snail:live hide resume} Out peeked Snail, dry as a daisy. {snail:face happy} "I told you." {all:face happy} {all:wobble} [proudly] "My house goes wherever I go."

es-ES.title: Caracol lleva su casa
es-ES.text: {canvas:clouds 0.7} [rushed] Llegaban nubes grises. ¡Iba a llover! Todos corrían a casa. {beaver:enter} Castor se paró junto a {snail:enter} Caracol. {beaver:go to snail} {beaver:face surprised} —¡Caracol! ¿Dónde está tu casa? {snail:face happy} {snail:live talk} —Aquí mismo —dijo Caracol. Pero Castor {beaver:live gnaw} le royó un palo para hacerle un tejadito. —Por si acaso —dijo, y {beaver:go away} se fue corriendo a su casa. {badger:enter} {badger:go to snail} Luego llegó Tejón. {badger:face surprised} —¡Caracol! ¿Dónde está tu casa? —Aquí mismo. Pero Tejón {badger:live dig} le cavó un agujerito. —Por si acaso —dijo, y {badger:go away} se fue corriendo a su madriguera. {bird:enter} {bird:go to snail} Pájaro bajó volando. {bird:face surprised} —¡Caracol! ¿Dónde está tu casa? [giggles] {snail:live laugh} —¡Aquí MISMO! —dijo Caracol. {bird:go away} Y Pájaro voló a su nido. {canvas:rain 0.8} {sfx:rain} Plic, plic, ploc, empezó a llover. {snail:live hide hold} Caracol se metió en su concha. {sfx:taps} Toc, toc, sonaba la lluvia en su tejado. {canvas:rain stop} {canvas:clouds stop} {canvas:sunshine} Cuando paró de llover y salió el sol, {beaver:go back} {badger:go back} {bird:go back} volvieron sus amigos. {badger:face sad} [gently] —¿Caracol? ¿Te has mojado? {snail:live hide resume} Caracol asomó la cabeza, sin una gota encima. {snail:face happy} —Ya os lo decía yo. {all:face happy} {all:wobble} [proudly] Mi casa va conmigo a todas partes.
